original_question: For holomorphic foliations on compact Kähler manifolds whose leaves have dimension greater than 1, what is the correct replacement for directed ddc-closed currents of bi-dimension (1,1) used in the one-dimensional case, so that one can develop an ergodic theory for such foliations?
target_in_paper: Problem 10.1 in §10, Ergodic theory for foliations with leaves of higher dimension: it asks for the right notion that should replace directed dd^c-closed currents from the one-dimensional case when the leaves have dimension greater than 1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's actual target very closely: the setting is holomorphic foliations on compact Kähler manifolds, the leaves have complex dimension greater than 1, the reference point is the one-dimensional/Riemann-surface case, and the aim is to identify the replacement for directed dd^c-closed currents needed to build an ergodic theory. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
missing_details: The paper explicitly allows the foliation to have singularities; it is not restricted to the nonsingular case. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
The ambient compact Kähler manifold X is understood to come with a fixed Kähler form ω. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

The comparison case is specifically foliations by Riemann surfaces, for which the paper recalls the existence of a positive dd^c-closed current of bidimension (1,1) directed by the foliation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

The local motivation for asking for a new notion is that even the product of two foliations by Riemann surfaces need not admit a positive dd^c-closed current directed by the product foliation; so the paper is not merely asking for a formal higher-bidimension analogue. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

The paper is asking for the correct substitute notion itself, not yet for a theorem about existence, uniqueness, classification, or convergence properties of such objects. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
refined_question: Let F be a holomorphic foliation, possibly with singularities, on a compact Kähler manifold X endowed with a fixed Kähler form ω, and assume that the leaves of F have complex dimension greater than 1. In the case of foliations by Riemann surfaces, positive dd^c-closed currents of bidimension (1,1) directed by F are the basic objects used in the ergodic theory. What is the correct higher-dimensional directed notion that should replace these currents when the leaves have dimension greater than 1, in a way that still permits the development of an ergodic theory for F? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
justification: The draft is essentially a near-paraphrase of Problem 10.1. Section 10 first fixes the precise ambient data, then recalls the one-dimensional model case, and immediately asks for the right substitute in higher leaf dimension. The sentence just before Problem 10.1 explains why a naive extension is problematic: product foliations by Riemann surfaces may fail to admit directed positive dd^c-closed currents of the expected sort. So the sharp paper-faithful refinement is a fully explicit restatement of Problem 10.1, not a broader neighboring question such as Problem 10.2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
